purpose: Empty Shipyard II interior background for compositing the selected live 3D ship model; no ship is baked into this image.
prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: reusable opaque landscape game background plate for a live 3D ship construction viewer.
Edit the supplied Shipyard II interior into an EMPTY, GENERIC assembly bay. The game will render a real interchangeable 3D ship over this image (an interceptor, freighter, corvette, etc.). Absolutely no ship or ship-specific parts should be baked into the background.

Preserve the recognizable Shipyard II interior: weathered gray steel, chunky pale structural columns, yellow overhead crane rails, warm amber work lights, restrained cyan wall indicators, pipes, rear service wall and mezzanine, industrial floor, semi-realistic polished game-art rendering. Keep the same wide landscape aspect ratio and broadly the same elevated three-quarter interior camera and lighting.

Remove ALL spacecraft, hull frames, cargo pods, cockpits, engine housings, suspended ship panels, loose ship components and welding effects, in BOTH the main bay and neighboring bay. Remove their shadows, reflections and silhouettes. Rebuild the newly revealed background coherently, including the floor and rear wall.

Crucial composition for later 3D compositing: create one broad EMPTY central work area with a low, flat, continuous dark steel service deck, subtle floor seams and flush guide rails. Use a generic rectangular work zone with a restrained yellow border. It must accommodate many ship silhouettes rather than a narrow cradle sized for the previous freighter. Keep approximately the central 65 percent of the picture's width and the middle/lower 60 percent of its height free of tall equipment and foreground obstructions. There should be generous vertical headroom above that central deck. No uprights, clamps, robotic arms or railings crossing through the central volume where the rendered ship will appear. Keep the deck understated enough that a ship overlay will remain the focal point.

Retract crane hooks and hoists near the ceiling along the upper edge. Park folded robotic arms and maintenance equipment against the outer side walls, outside the clear central area. Replace the large foreground machinery with low, unobtrusive floor edge details so it cannot appear incorrectly behind a ship composited on top. Any neighboring bay is also empty and visually secondary. Keep useful environmental depth and convincing perspective, but avoid busy detail in the ship placement area. Use even soft task light on the empty deck, cool ambient fill and warm perimeter lighting; no object-shaped painted shadow in the center.

No ship, no spacecraft silhouette, no hull skeleton, no engine, no cockpit, no suspended panel, no crew, no people, no text, no labels, no numbers, no logos, no watermark, no UI, no progress bars, no placeholder wireframe, no illustrative diagram, no starfield, no transparent hole. Output one clean, finished, full-bleed empty hangar background image, not a mockup of the eventual ship viewer.
